columns.title: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 49.2 on Thanksgiving, and the rest of this league should be embarrassed
columns.dek: Allen-tents & Purposes has 133.74 before Black Friday. Everybody else is playing for second.
body: Let me tell you what Thanksgiving looked like from the RedDevil904 couch. Jahmyr Gibbs: 205 rushing yards, three touchdowns, five catches, 49.2 points. DeVonta Smith: 11 catches, 200 yards, two touchdowns, 45.0. D'Andre Swift: 29.2. That's 123.4 points from three players, on a Thursday, while the turkey was still resting.

Allen-tents & Purposes was already the best team in this league. It's 8‑3, it scores 140.2 a week, it has an 89‑32 all-play and it's at 91 percent for a bye. And Josh Allen scored 3.54. Think about that. The quarterback had his worst day of the year and the team still has 133.74 with three starters to go.

I'm hearing DeVonta Smith has asked RedDevil904 for the locker right next to Jahmyr Gibbs so they can compare box scores. Word is he loves the vibe on Allen-tents & Purposes, thinks it's the best room in the league, and has told people he's never going back to a team that starts him at flex.

Meanwhile, the rest of you. Your Mom’s Magic Dick has 19.60. JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson has 0.00. I Pulled My McCaff, the second-best team on paper, is losing to Bill_Buttlicker. So here's the column in one line for everyone not named RedDevil904. YOU'RE ALL PLAYING FOR SECOND!

columns.title: Black Friday film: Pittsburgh's defense graded, and so is the guy who benched it
columns.dek: Eight league players on the tape from Pittsburgh. One defense scored 28. It started for nobody.
body: Black Friday tape. Denver at Pittsburgh. Eight league starters and one very expensive bench. Grades are final.

Jonah Coleman. Eight catches, 15.2 for Allen-tents & Purposes. Ran 26 yards on the ground and did his job in the pass game. Grade: B. DK Metcalf. Three catches, a touchdown, 12.6 for Slippery Balls. Grade: B. Jaylen Waddle. Five for 53, 10.3 for JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson. Grade: C-plus. Pat Bryant. Four for 42, 8.2 for YourMomsGivin’ Bijan’s. Grade: C.

Jaylen Warren. 46 yards, 5.6, and it was enough to put I Pulled My McCaff back in front. Grade: C, with a bonus for timing. The Denver defense. 7.0 for PickensMyPukaHurts!. Grade: C. Bo Nix. 169 yards, two picks, a lost fumble, 1.46 for bo’sBENdingyouover😘😘. Grade: F.

The Pittsburgh defense. Two interceptions, a fumble recovery, three sacks, two touchdowns, 3 points allowed. 28.0. Grade: A-plus. The manager who left it on the bench for Tampa Bay was Bill_Buttlicker. Grade: F. No curve. I don't care who signs the column.

Word around the Pittsburgh facility is that the Steelers defense has asked to be moved off the McCallyCockin(his butt) bench and onto a roster where 28 points counts. I'm told the unit has no problem with Bill_Buttlicker personally. It just watched the box score like everybody else.

columns.title: Five Black Friday moves from a strategist who has never once lost a Friday
columns.dek: Seven league starters play in Pittsburgh tonight. Here's how to handle them, numbered, for your convenience.
body: Thanksgiving is in the books and the professionals are back at work. Denver plays at Pittsburgh tonight with seven league starters, and most of you have no plan. I have five.

1. Skatabooboo: you have 3.90 and eight starters left. The only way to guarantee the score doesn't go down is to stop starting people. Bench everybody for Sunday. A score you can't lose is a score you can't lose. 2. JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson: you're at 0.00, which is technically the best defense in the league. Jaylen Waddle plays tonight. Consider benching him to protect the shutout.

3. Hing1eMcCring13berry: you trail by 0.60. Jaylen Warren is your only player tonight, and one good drive puts you ahead. Do not watch. Watching is how momentum gets jinxed. 4. tballsmccall: new team name, new you. Start Bo Nix, obviously, and when he scores, take the credit for naming the team after him. Correlation is causation if you post it first. 5. ChuckJ10: the Denver defense has the whole night to itself. Root for zero points against, and also root for Bo Nix. Hedging is a sign of maturity.

Sources say Bo Nix has heard about bo’sBENdingyouover😘😘 and has quietly asked his agent whether he can be traded to a roster with a name his parents can say out loud. I'm told tballsmccall took it as a compliment and has no plans to change it before the Week 11 video gets posted, which means never.

columns.title: The Bench Regret Index has a new league leader, and he signs my checks
columns.dek: 28.0 points on the bench, 5.00 behind, and a model that does not care about feelings.
body: New metric. The Bench Regret Index takes the best score on a team's bench and subtracts the team's current deficit. McCallyCockin(his butt): Pittsburgh defense 28.0 on the bench, down 5.00. Regret Index: 23.0, the highest in the league. bo’sBENdingyouover😘😘: Sam LaPorta 14.4 on the bench, down 40.64. Index: negative 26.24, which means the bench couldn't have saved it, which the model scores as peace.

The conclusion is obvious. Benches should not score points. Teams with high Bench Regret lose the matchup 69 percent of the time, per a live model I ran this morning on exactly one matchup. That's a sample size of one, which is the most honest sample size there is. It can't be biased. There's nobody else in it.

Allen-tents & Purposes has Khalil Shakir at 6.3 on the bench and leads by 129.34. Regret Index: negative 123.04. I've never seen a number that calm. RedDevil904 should be studied. I'd study him, but the model already knows everything.

I have it on good authority that Christian McCaffrey has asked Hing1eMcCring13berry for a bigger share of the team name, since he's already got the McCaff part and would like the rest. Sources say he likes the vibe in the I Pulled My McCaff locker room and has no complaints about the manager, only about the punctuation.

Bottom line: I Pulled My McCaff by 17.5 is still the pick, the live number says 69 percent, and Bill_Buttlicker's bench outscored Tampa Bay's 7.79 projection by roughly three touchdowns. The model has spoken. It doesn't take questions.
